message.abstract: <jats:p>Short-term wind power forecasting up to 72 h ahead is essential for secure power system operation and efficient electricity market participation under high renewable penetration. However, accurate forecasting at both turbine and wind-farm levels remains challenging because operational numerical weather prediction (NWP) products are substantially coarser than the spatial and temporal scales at which within-farm flow heterogeneity, turbine interactions, and wake effects occur. Existing studies mainly focus either on direct power-series forecasting or on spatial estimation under given inflow conditions, and rarely address coarse-NWP-to-turbine state reconstruction and multi-step power forecasting within a unified framework. To address this gap, this study formulates short-term wind power forecasting as a multi-scale partially observed dynamical system and proposes a two-stage framework. First, a spatiotemporal physics-guided graph neural network (PGNN) super-resolves coarse NWP inputs into turbine-level wind speeds by embedding wake-consistent directed interactions and turbine layout information into a turbine graph. Second, a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) performs parallel multi-step forecasting across turbines by integrating super-resolved wind speeds, historical SCADA power, and turbine-specific static covariates. Farm-level forecasts are then obtained through hierarchical aggregation. Case studies on two real-world wind farms with different terrain characteristics show that the proposed PGNN--TFT framework consistently outperforms representative baselines in both deterministic and probabilistic forecasting metrics. The results indicate that explicitly reconstructing turbine-scale wind states from coarse NWP before temporal forecasting is more effective than direct power forecasting alone, providing a physically grounded and scalable solution for multi-scale short-term wind power forecasting.</jats:p>
title: Advancing short-term wind power forecasting via Physics-Guided Graph Neural Networks for super-resolving Numerical Weather Prediction
